inherited_summary: Born in San Juan Zitlaltepec, State of Mexico. Working-class family. Father worked construction. Navarrete worked as a bricklayer (albañil) for 3 years alongside training. Only completed primary and secondary school. Active economic disadvantage.
ecosystem_summary: Uncle/coach Pedro Navarrete (also a boxer) trained him from age 7. Boxing family — brothers Jhonny and Pedro also boxed. Modest local gyms with no sponsors. Mexican small-club boxing circuit. Limited early resources but strong family boxing tradition.

endowment_summary: World champion at 19 (youngest Japanese wrestler ever), Olympic gold at 22. Won 5 straight national elementary titles from 2nd-6th grade. Started wrestling at 4. Prodigy-level wrestling ability from extremely young age — trajectory-changing.
inherited_summary: Father Seiya was a former wrestler who set up a home wrestling room in their apartment and coached both sons. Working-class family. Father's wrestling knowledge was key but family had limited resources — 8-tatami room home dojo.
ecosystem_summary: Father as coach with homemade home dojo. Older brother Keisuke (also 2020 Olympian) as training partner. JOC Elite Academy in Tokyo from junior high. Yamanashi Gakuin University. Japan Self-Defense Forces Physical Training School. Strong Japanese wrestling pipeline.
